solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prudish doctor startled CIA

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic gives the American spy agency a fright, and is a bit of a prude about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun, a medic; here it is a verb meaning to tamper with, so STARTLED and CIA are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strait-laced holds rigid, old-fashioned moral views, which is what prudish describes.

clue.text: In which money may be kept tied up, you say?

definitions.text: In which money may be kept

indicators.note: an invitation to hear the word spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: trussed means bound tightly, like a chicken for roasting

explanation.surface: A question about where cash is locked away, and whether it is tied up in investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tied up' reads as money committed long-term, but it is TRUSSED, which sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust is a legal arrangement holding money or property on someone's behalf, often until they come of age.

clue.text: Made sauna boiling time after time

indicators.note: boiling water churns about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps heating the sauna to scalding point again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means to the point of sickness, used of something repeated endlessly, over and over.

clue.text: Songbird perching on top of church, a little one

indicators.note: in a down answer, the bird sits above the next piece

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird, such as the blue tit

explanation.surface: A small bird sits on a church roof, a tiny one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little one' sounds like a further description of the bird, but it is the definition: titch is British slang for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is informal British slang for a small person or child, a little one.

clue.text: Article about northern woman

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerning a woman from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a common female first name, so the clue's woman stands for it.

clue.text: Unpredictable boy catching rodent

indicators.note: the boy's name holds the rodent inside it, as if having caught it

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A capricious boy who is busy trapping a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is irregular and inconsistent, so it cannot be forecast.

clue.text: Scout cooking with Primus? Yummy!

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scout making dinner on a camping stove, and it tastes delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: A Primus is a brand of portable paraffin camping stove, natural kit for a Scout.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumptious is an informal word for delicious, the same as yummy.

clue.text: Beardless son in spotless shelter

indicators.note: the son's letter goes inside the pair of words that follow

parts.note: spotless means clean
a haven is a place of shelter or refuge

explanation.surface: A man without a beard has a son living in an immaculate refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone freshly shaved has no beard or stubble at all.

clue.text: Half of church service makes you heave

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Half a church service is enough to make you feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a church service; it is one of the armed services, the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: When your stomach churns it lurches with nausea, as when you heave or retch.

clue.text: Pretend Rilke's got this curly hair?

indicators.note: the words before contain this one, so the answer is tucked inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Was the German poet Rilke wearing fake curls?
explanation.walkthrough: Rainer Maria Rilke was a German-language poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender curling stem of a climbing plant, and by extension a thin curl or wisp of hair.

clue.text: Peacekeepers felt in perfect condition

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
felt means touched with the hand

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops felt they were in top form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' reads as experienced an emotion; here it is the past tense of feel, touched.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never handled or damaged is pristine, still in mint condition.

clue.text: Stupidly derailed Victor, a reckless type

indicators.note: acting stupidly means doing things in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Victor foolishly wrecked a train, showing what a risk-taker he is.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is someone who takes wild, dangerous risks for thrills.

clue.text: Drug put in army's drink

indicators.note: the drug's letter is placed inside the army's abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone spikes the soldiers' drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a drink, the classic British cuppa.

clue.text: Crowded, as lunch may be?

definitions.meaning: a ... lunch is one made at home and carried in a box or bag

explanation.surface: Crowded, as lunch may be?
explanation.definitionFit: A packed room is full to bursting, and a packed lunch is prepared and boxed to take out.

clue.text: Scientific man Nietzsche mistrusted to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The German philosopher Nietzsche was partly suspicious of a man of science.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is a scientist who studies substances and their reactions.

clue.text: Summary that's almost exact

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: precise means exact

explanation.surface: A summary that gets things nearly right.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a short summary of a longer text.

clue.text: Diaries occasionally displaying anger

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone's diaries now and then show bursts of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath or fury.

clue.text: Histrionics alarmed Mo terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mo was so frightened that a big theatrical scene followed.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodrama is exaggerated, over-emotional behaviour, the same as histrionics.

clue.text: Yours truly's following lake north of Italian border

indicators.note: the setter's own piece comes after the lake's letter
in a down answer, the earlier pieces sit above the next one

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying I, and the 's makes I am, contracted

explanation.surface: The setter stands behind a lake that lies just north of the Italian frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is the setter, I; with 's (is, or here am) it becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or edge, the same as a border.

clue.text: Concede Her Majesty must retire in time

indicators.note: the turned royal letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so in a down answer the letters run upwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen gives way and agrees it is time for her to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must retire' reads as the monarch abdicating, but it is the reversal signal; in a down answer the royal letters read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to a point is to concede it, admitting the other side is right.

clue.text: Outfit for the tango follower?

definitions.meaning: a set of standard clothes worn by members of a group, like a school's
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the word for T is followed by the word for U

explanation.surface: Something to wear for the dancer who follows in the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tango' is the dance, but here it is T in the NATO alphabet, whose next code word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform is a set of matching clothes, an outfit, and is also the NATO code word for U, coming after T.

clue.text: Row after pig has head chopped off

indicators.note: the first letter of the animal's name is removed

parts.note: a boar is a male or wild pig

explanation.surface: A dispute breaks out after a pig is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it means propel a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is the blade you row with, and to oar is an old verb meaning to row.

clue.text: Vicar taken aback by extremely strange poem

indicators.note: the next piece sits beside it
aback means backwards, so the title is read in reverse

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A vicar is startled by something very odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprised; it reverses REV to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is poetry, and a verse can be a single poem.

clue.text: Second right-wing bank clerk is a liar

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party
a teller is a bank clerk who serves customers at the counter

explanation.surface: A Conservative bank clerk who is a fibber.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller of tall tales is a euphemism for someone who tells lies, a fibber.
